On a build server, a consistently elevated load average typically signals that compilation jobs and tests are saturating available resources. While parallel compilers like Make, Ninja, and Gradle intentionally push load averages above the physical core count to hide I/O latency, excessively high values lead to severe context-switching overhead and thrashing. If disk or network operations become bottlenecks during artifact generation, processes will accumulate in uninterruptible wait states and drive queue lengths even higher, ultimately extending build durations and causing pipeline delays.
